notes.s: A victory lap aimed squarely at everyone who said they would fail.
notes.t: The Steve Aoki remix of a Love Yourself 承 Her B-side gave the group their first Billboard Hot 100 entry that mattered, and the song works as the receipt for the class insults in 뱁새 and 불타오르네. Suga wrote the opening spoon line as a direct answer to being called a dirt spoon. The trash talk is dense with Korean-only references, including ticketing slang and a four-character idiom, so English versions read much flatter than the original. The mic-drop moment at the 2017 AMAs is where most non-Korean fans arrived.
k: 포도 is a grape, and in Korean ticketing slang it is an insult. On the seat maps at Interpark an unsold seat shows as a purple dot, so a chart full of them looks like a bunch of grapes and a 포도밭, a vineyard, is a show nobody bought. Claiming your concerts never have grapes is claiming they sell out on sight. No amount of dictionary work gets you there.

배가 아프다 is a stomach ache and also the standard idiom for envy, from the proverb about your cousin buying land. 고소해 then runs three ways: sue me, it tastes nutty, and the colloquial serves you right, which is delicious. Sue me is primary, with the gloating sense riding underneath. Korean insult writing stacks homophones like this deliberately.

사필귀정 is 事必歸正, a four-character Sino-Korean idiom meaning everything eventually comes back around to what is right. 네 글자 means four characters, and Korean counts these idioms by syllable, which is why the category is called 사자성어, four-character phrase. Announcing the count before delivering the phrase is the setup to the punchline.

학을 떼다 means to be thoroughly done with something after a bad time of it. The 학 is 瘧, malaria, and the image is shaking the fever off, so it is far stronger than 싫어하다: they have been through it and never want to again. Spelled with 떼다, to detach, not 때다.

vocab.note: 금수저 gold spoon and 흙수저 dirt spoon are the mid-2010s shorthand for the family you were born into
Rough slang, and separately the verb for chopping firewood
Applied to people it means mature, so half-cooked ones are the immature ones
Also means to ignore a message on purpose, left on read
Industry word for getting someone onto a show or a bill
만끽하다 is to savour something to the very limit
효도하다 is doing right by your parents; the verse hands the job to a sibling to cover

vocab.en: be full of, be packed with

vocab.note: The suffix -빛 means the colour or light of: 은빛 silver, 핏빛 blood red
도망가다 or 도망치다 to run away
모잘라 in the lyric is the colloquial squeeze of it
말 조심 watch your mouth, 발 조심 watch your step, 몸조심 take care of yourself
Always derogatory, so 그 꼴 나지 means you will end up looking like that
폼 is the English form; the whole word is 2010s slang
